claims.claim_summary: **BRAIZ Works Research** **WP-06 · Version 1.0.0 · September 24, 2026**  > Public-safe research.
claims.section: Measuring speed only after scope, complexity, quality, evidence, and recovery are held constant

claims.claim_summary: AI productivity claims are easy to inflate when faster work is compared with a weaker result.
A faster result is not automatically a better production system.
claims.section: Why raw speed is a weak metric

claims.claim_summary: A defensible compression claim requires an equal-output contract.
A useful enterprise comparison can separate three lanes:        The purpose is not to guarantee that one lane always wins.
AI systems can compress active human effort without compressing wall-clock time, or vice versa.
claims.section: Wall time and person-hours are different

claims.claim_summary: Actual spend, replacement cost, and modeled savings answer different questions.
Once equal scope and quality are established, compression can become powerful evidence.
claims.section: Quality-normalized compression as an enterprise proof

claims.claim_summary: Before publishing a productivity multiplier, disclose the compared scope, quality controls, evidence strength, time basis, cost basis, sample size, and major limitations.
claims.section: A publication checklist for productivity claims

claims.claim_summary: Counterfactual labor and cost estimates remain models unless directly observed.
